summary: editable-contracts 0.0.16 ships preinstall alternate-runtime dropper executing obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs is an obfuscated loader (hex-mangled identifiers, string-array indirection) that checks for a local `bun` binary and, if absent, downloads Bun v1.3.13 from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases into a temp directory, chmod +x's it, and invokes it against the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line string-array-obfuscated blob (@bun-cjs header, rotator function pushing/shifting a large index array) that is not required or imported by the library's declared main (dist/editable-contracts.js). The package advertises itself as ServiceTitan's `editable-contracts` TypeScript form-editing library (repository servicetitan/editable-contracts), but the preinstall hook, setup.mjs, and math_init.js do not exist in the upstream source tree — consistent with a trojanized publish of the legitimate name. Fetching an alien language runtime at preinstall solely to execute a bundled opaque payload is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern; `npm install editable-contracts` yields arbitrary attacker-controlled code execution on the installer host with no consent.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
